summary.headline: Lupin Q4 FY26 revenue rose 32% YoY to Rs 7,475 crore and EBITDA 68% to Rs 2,171 crore; FY27 guided to high-single-digit growth and ~25% margin.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 was the 15th consecutive quarter of YoY growth, with record sales and profitability; EBITDA margin was 29.4% (ex forex and other income), up 620 bps YoY. FY26 revenue rose 23% to Rs 27,958 crore and EBITDA reached Rs 8,160 crore at a 29.7% margin, above the 27-28% guidance. Q4 EBITDA moved down QoQ, which management attributed to the Mirabegron settlement payment to Astellas, forex and higher manpower cost booked in other expenses. Management guided FY27 to high-single-digit revenue growth (in rupee terms) and around 25% EBITDA margin, citing Tolvaptan and Mirabegron competition, higher R&D (~8% of sales) and a 25-26% ETR.

segments.name: US
segments.commentary: Q4 sales USD 371 million (+6% QoQ cc); FY26 USD 1,318 million (+40% cc), driven by Tolvaptan (sole generic), Mirabegron, Risperdal Consta and base volumes, partly offset by low-single-digit price erosion (Albuterol, Suprep).

segments.name: India
segments.commentary: Q4 Rs 1,908 crore (+11.5%), core prescription +14.5% vs IPM 11.6%; FY26 Rs 8,114 crore (+7.1%), with diabetes slowed to 9.4% growth vs 12.2% category due to loss of exclusivity on in-licensed products. In-licensed share fell to ~6% of portfolio from 12%.

segments.name: Other Developed Markets
segments.commentary: Europe, Canada and Australia: Q4 Rs 845 crore (+7.1%, 12% of sales); FY26 Rs 3,244 crore (+13.3%, 11% of sales). European sales passed USD 200 million; VISUfarma acquisition to be consolidated from FY27 Q1.

segments.name: Emerging Markets
segments.commentary: Q4 Rs 991 crore (+49%), led by Brazil (+113% YoY in local currency on Dapagliflozin), South Africa, Mexico and Philippines; FY26 Rs 3,483 crore (+35.2%).

segments.name: GIB
segments.commentary: FY26 growth of 11.8%; Q4 India GIB saw lower tender sales, per management.

guidance_outlook: FY27: high-single-digit revenue growth in rupee terms, with EBITDA margin around 25%; management says the budget was set about three months ago and includes Tolvaptan and Mirabegron competition and higher R&D.
R&D to be around 8% of sales in FY27.
FY27 effective tax rate of about 25-26% due to phasing out of incentives on some domestic facilities.
US: management expects FY27 US revenue to be above USD 1 billion, with high-single-digit to low-double-digit erosion vs FY26 in a base case, offset by injectables and Pegfilgrastim.
India: expects to outperform IPM by 1.2x-1.3x and plans about 20 product launches in FY27.
Mirabegron amortisation of USD 75 million settlement spread over the next two years; per-unit cost factored into gross margin.
capex_capacity: US pipeline: 50+ launches planned over three years, including 10 exclusive first-to-files, four biosimilars and two to three 505(b)(2)s; 8-9 respiratory filings planned in FY27, including Respimat and Etanercept biosimilar.

Launches expected in FY27: Ravicti (GPB) as a material product, Saxenda in H2 FY27, Sacubitril/Valsartan and Rivaroxaban (first-to-file), Pegfilgrastim ramping from Q2-Q3 (partnership with Valorum), Ranibizumab later in FY27, Dalbavancin 505(b)(2).
FY28: full-year Pegfilgrastim and Ranibizumab, Dulera (responding to FDA query), Apixaban 505(b)(2) new dosage form.
Pegfilgrastim on-body injector: filing this fiscal year, launch in FY28 or FY29 depending on FDA approval.
Pithampur unit 2 remediation on track; Goa EIR and VAI status received in Q4 FY26.
Specialty M&A: VISUfarma acquired (Italy, Spain added to UK, Germany, France); management sees a high flow of ophthalmology assets and is also looking at pulmonology and rare neuro.
demand_pricing: Tolvaptan: generic penetration under 40%, with a third competitor expected around the September patent expiry, which is included in plans. Mirabegron: penetration near 50%; a third player that settled with Astellas has not yet entered, awaiting supply; competition is expected in FY27.
Spiriva: management is not certain of generic competition in FY27 despite some filings.
Albuterol: GSK's branded green inhaler (Ventolin version) expected around Q3 FY27; management does not expect adverse impact.

Semaglutide India: launched as Semanex and Livarise; ranked number 2 among generics and number 3 overall in the branded-generic market within about a month. Management expects Brazil and Canada filings this year.
Risperdal Consta: demand exceeds supply; CMO ramp-up has been a constraint, and Teva also has supplier issues.

Biosimilars: current franchise about USD 50 million (largely partner-led royalty/profit share), expected to grow multiple times this fiscal year. Management says new entrants are not expected to change economics for first-wave, limited-competitor products.
Freight: ocean freight about 15% higher, air freight about 60% higher; raw material and solvent availability issues; price increases possible but not quantified.

qa_highlights.question: Is the FY27 guidance (high-single-digit growth, ~25% margin) factoring in Tolvaptan and Mirabegron competition?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes, both Tolvaptan and Mirabegron competition is factored in; the margin decline is attributed to these competitors and higher R&D.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Q4 EBITDA fall QoQ?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to higher manpower cost, the Mirabegron settlement payment to Astellas booked in other expenses, and forex; the impact was in other expenses, not the US business itself.

qa_highlights.question: What is the US revenue outlook for FY27 and FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said FY27 US revenue should be above USD 1 billion, with high-single-digit to low-double-digit erosion in base case, offset by launches; FY28 was not quantified.

qa_highlights.question: Will the Mirabegron settlement affect margins going forward?
qa_highlights.answer: Part is a variable per-unit cost in gross margin and part is a USD 75 million amortisation over about two years; the split depends on sales.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of Ranibizumab and Pegfilgrastim?
qa_highlights.answer: Ranibizumab to launch later in FY27 with both pre-filled syringe and vial; Pegfilgrastim on-body filing this year with FY28 or FY29 launch; Pegfilgrastim partnered with Valorum.

qa_highlights.question: What is the biosimilar pricing outlook as more entrants arrive?
qa_highlights.answer: Management focuses on first-wave or limited-competitor products; it expects new entrants to help overall biosimilar economics rather than erode them further.

qa_highlights.question: How is Semaglutide launch in India tracking?
qa_highlights.answer: Early but solid; ranked number 2 generic and number 3 overall after about nine days, with April data pending; the company aims to be a top-3 generic player.

risks_watch: Tolvaptan: third competitor expected around the September patent expiry, already in plans; generic penetration under 40%.
Mirabegron: third settled player yet to enter (awaiting supply); USD 75 million settlement amortisation over about two years plus a variable per-unit cost that depends on sales.
FY27 margin guide of ~25% vs FY26 29.7%; ETR rising to 25-26% and R&D around 8% of sales are key drags to monitor.
Freight (ocean ~15%, air ~60% higher), raw material and solvent availability; price increases possible but not quantified by management.
Semaglutide India: early launch (about nine days of data at the time of call); April data pending; competitive pressure from Zydus pen.
Pithampur unit 2 remediation still in progress; Ellipta filings delayed on product PK; Risperdal Consta supply constrained by CMO ramp-up.
Other operating income (PLI export benefit) fell 21% YoY in Q4; management expects some PLI to return next year.
key_quotes: This quarter marked our 15 th consecutive quarter of year over year growth with highest ever sales and profitability.
As mentioned in our earlier interactions, we expect to grow our top line high-single digits with margins at around 25% in FY27, despite increased headwinds from an uncertain geopolitical environment.
We have factored that in both competition for Mirabegron as well as Tolvaptan.
Clearly that is impacting everybody these are dark clouds on the horizon .
It's about USD 50 million right now but slated to be multiple times this financial year itself.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the FY26 print and the FY27 framework (high-single-digit rupee revenue growth, ~25% margin), but cautious and non-committal on specifics: management declined to quantify freight and raw material inflation, gave FY28 US revenue no number, and called Semaglutide "very early days". Answers on Q4 EBITDA decline were direct, attributing it to other expenses (Mirabegron settlement, forex, manpower, M&A costs).

adds.what: Pegfilgrastim on-body injector (filing this fiscal year; launch FY28 or FY29 depending on FDA approval) - product launch, not clearly productive capacity

growth.why: FY27 guided to high-single-digit rupee revenue growth (midpoint ~8%) and ~25% EBITDA margin, backed by 50+ US launch pipeline, ~20 India launches, US sales guided above USD 1bn and India outperformance of 1.2-1.3x IPM; no new manufacturing capacity quantified, so backing is partial.
